Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 52–57 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿nor any messenger or prophet﴾. It has been said: the messenger (rasul) is one who is sent to the creation by the sending of Jibril to him face to face, and speaking with him directly, while the prophet (nabi) is one to whom it comes by inspiration (ilham) or in a dream.

It has also been said: the messenger is one sent with a law (shar') and commanded to convey it, while the prophet is one commanded to call to the law of one before him, and no book was revealed to him. Both of them necessarily require a manifest miracle (mu'jizah). ﴿Except when he desires, Satan casts into his desire﴾. The meaning of tamanna (desires) is: he yearns for something and prepares in his soul what he wishes for.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes have said that the meaning of tamanna is recited (talā).

The group of exegetes said concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse: when the crowd's turning away from him weighed heavily upon him, he (ﷺ) wished in himself that nothing would descend upon him that would repel them from him, out of his eagerness for their faith. One day he was sitting in one of their assemblies, and the surah (wa'l-Najm idha hawa) [al-Najm: 1] had been revealed to him, so he began to recite it to them until he reached his saying: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [al-Najm: 19–20]. That wish was in his soul, so there flowed upon his tongue what Satan had cast upon him: "Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for." When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went on with his recitation until he finished the surah. When he prostrated at its end, all those in the assembly, Muslims and polytheists, prostrated with him. Then Quraysh dispersed, delighted with that, saying: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods with the best mention." Then Jibril came to him and said: "What have you done? You recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved and feared a great fear, so Allah revealed this verse. Thus they said.

None of this is authentic, nor is it established by any means, and with its lack of authenticity, indeed its falsehood, the verifiers have refuted it by the Book of Allah, the Exalted. Allah says: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–46]. (p-970) And His saying: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3], and His saying: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. Thus He negated even the approach to inclination, let alone inclination.

Al-Bazzar said: this is a report we do not know to be narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) with a connected chain.

Al-Bayhaqi said: this story is not established in terms of transmission; then he began to speak about the narrators of this story being criticized.

Imam al-A'immah Ibn Khuzaymah said: this story is a fabrication of the zanadiqah (heretics).

Qadi Iyad said in al-Shifa': the Community has unanimously agreed that in matters concerning conveyance, he is protected from reporting anything contrary to what he is, neither intentionally, nor deliberately, nor by forgetfulness, nor by error.

Ibn Kathir said: many exegetes have mentioned here the story of the cranes, and of the return of many of the emigrants to the land of Abyssinia, thinking that the polytheists of Quraysh had embraced Islam. But all its routes are mursal (broken in the chain), and I have not seen it transmitted with a connected chain from any sound path.

When the falsehood of that has been established for you, you know that the meaning of tamanna is recited and read, as we have mentioned from al-Wahidi's report on that from the exegetes.

Likewise al-Baghawi said: most exegetes said the meaning of tamanna is recited and read the Book of Allah, and the meaning of ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ is into his recitation and reading.

Ibn Jarir said: this view is closer to the interpretation of the speech, and what preceded in the explanation of His saying: ﴿They know not the Book except wishful thinking (amani)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 78] supports this. It has also been said: the meaning of tamanna is "spoke," and the meaning of ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ is into his speech; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. And it has been said: the meaning of tamanna is "said."

The summary of the meaning of the verse: Satan put that into the ears of the polytheists without the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaking it, nor it running upon his tongue. So this verse is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning: let that not terrify you nor grieve you, for the like of this has befallen those before you among the messengers and prophets. And on the assumption that the meaning of tamanna is "he spoke to himself," as related by al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i, for both said: "tamanna" means when he speaks to himself, then the meaning is: when he speaks to himself with something, Satan speaks it and casts it into the ears of the people, without the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaking it or it running upon his tongue.

Ibn Atiyyah said: there is no disagreement that Satan's casting is only into audible words by which the trial occurs.

It has been said concerning the interpretation of the verse: the intended "cranes" are the angels, and this is refuted by His saying: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾, i.e., nullifies it, and the intercession of the angels is not false.

It has been said: that ran upon his tongue (ﷺ) through forgetfulness and oblivion, and both are permissible for the prophets; but it is refuted by the fact that forgetfulness and oblivion are not permissible in matters concerning conveyance, as is established in its proper places. Then, when Allah the Exalted consoled him with this consolation, and that it had befallen those before him among the messengers and prophets, He made clear that He nullifies that and does not confirm it, nor does Satan's deception with it persist. So He said: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾, i.e., nullifies it and makes it passing and not established, ﴿then Allah makes His verses firm﴾, i.e., establishes them, ﴿and Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾, i.e., abundant in knowledge and wisdom in all His sayings and deeds.

The clause ﴿that He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾ is for causation, i.e., that casting which Satan casts is a trial, i.e., misguidance, ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, i.e., doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿and the hard-hearted﴾ are the polytheists, for their hearts never soften to the truth, nor do they return to the right by any means. Then He, the Exalted, recorded against these two groups, those in whose hearts is a disease and those in whose hearts is hardness, that they are wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾, i.e., severe enmity. Describing the dissension as "far" is an intensification, and the one truly described by it is the one who holds it.

When He, the Exalted, made clear that this casting was a trial regarding the people of hypocrisy, doubt and polytheism, He made clear that for the believers who know Allah and recognize Him, it is a cause for them to attain knowledge that the Qur'an is truth and right. So He said: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾, i.e., the truth sent down from Him. It has been said that the pronoun in "that it" refers to Allah's empowering Satan to cast; because that is among the practices of His prophets. But this is refuted by His saying: ﴿so that they believe in it﴾, for the intended meaning of faith in the Qur'an is that they remain steadfast in faith in it, ﴿and their hearts humble themselves to it﴾, i.e., submit, are humbled and yield; for faith in it and the humbling of hearts to it cannot be an empowerment from Satan, but rather to the Qur'an. ﴿And indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe﴾ in the matters of their religion ﴿to a straight path﴾, i.e., a sound way with no crookedness.

Abu Haywah read (wa-inna Allaha li-hadin alladhina amanu) with tanwin.

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾, i.e., in doubt about the Qur'an. It has been said: about the religion, which the mention of the straight path indicates. It has been said: about Satan's casting, so they say: "Why did he mention the idols favorably and then retract that?" Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read (fi muriyah) with a damma on the mim. ﴿Until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., the Resurrection unexpectedly, suddenly, ﴿or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day﴾, and it is the Day of Resurrection, for there is no day after it, so on this account it is called barren. In the language, "barren" (aqim) is one who has no child; and since days follow one another, that was made like the condition of birth; and since no day comes after that day, it is described as barren. It has been said: it is a day of battle in which they are killed, like the day of Badr. It has been said: the day is described as barren because there is no compassion or mercy in it, so it is as if barren of good. From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 41], i.e., one in which there is no good and which brings no rain.

﴿The dominion on that day is for Allah﴾, i.e., the absolute sovereignty and complete control: on the Day of Resurrection, it belongs to Allah alone, with none contesting Him in it and none repelling Him from it. The clause ﴿He will judge between them﴾ is a resumed sentence answering an implied question. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif reported from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: Ibn Abbas used to read: "And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet or muhaddath (one spoken to)."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf the like of it, (p-971) and added: "then muhaddath was abrogated." He said: the muhaddathun are the companion of Ya-Sin, Luqman, the believer of Pharaoh's family, and the companion of Musa.

Al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah reported. al-Suyuti said with a chain whose transmitters are trustworthy, through Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [al-Najm: 19–20], 'Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for.' The polytheists rejoiced at that and said: he has mentioned our gods. Then Jibril came to him and said: recite to me what I brought you. So he recited: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza...﴾, 'Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for.' Jibril said: I did not bring you this; this is from Satan. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except when he desires...﴾ the verse."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported. al-Suyuti said with a sound chain from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited al-Najm in Makkah, and he mentioned something similar, but did not mention Ibn Abbas.

Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim reported it from Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi from Sa'id as a mursal (broken) report.

Abd ibn Humayd reported it from al-Suddi from Abu Salih as a mursal report.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported it from Ibn Shihab as a mursal report.

Ibn Jarir reported from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham something similar, also as a mursal report.

The conclusion is that all the reports on this subject are either mursal or munqati' (with breaks in the chain), and none of them establishes proof. We have already quoted from the hadith scholars at the beginning of this discussion what is sufficient. Whoever wishes to see all of its reports, let him consult al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti, though lengthening by mentioning them here would be of no benefit, for we have informed you that none of them together establishes proof.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When he desires, Satan casts into his desire﴾: "it means when he speaks, Satan casts into his speech."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Dahhak, who said: By tamanni he means recitation and reading; Satan cast into his desire: into his recitation. ﴿Then Allah abrogates﴾: Jibril abrogates by Allah's command what Satan cast upon the tongue of the Prophet.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding "when he desires": he spoke in his desire; he said: his speech.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah reported from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾: he said, the Day of Badr.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b something similar.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "a punishment of a barren day" — he said: it is the Day of Badr.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah the like of it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: "It is the Day of Resurrection, which has no night."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr the like of it.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Dahhak the like of it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 52–57 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿nor any messenger or prophet﴾. It has been said: the messenger (rasul) is one who is sent to the creation by the sending of Jibril to him face to face, and speaking with him directly, while the prophet (nabi) is one to whom it comes by inspiration (ilham) or in a dream.

It has also been said: the messenger is one sent with a law (shar') and commanded to convey it, while the prophet is one commanded to call to the law of one before him, and no book was revealed to him. Both of them necessarily require a manifest miracle (mu'jizah). ﴿Except when he desires, Satan casts into his desire﴾. The meaning of tamanna (desires) is: he yearns for something and prepares in his soul what he wishes for.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes have said that the meaning of tamanna is recited (talā).

The group of exegetes said concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse: when the crowd's turning away from him weighed heavily upon him, he (ﷺ) wished in himself that nothing would descend upon him that would repel them from him, out of his eagerness for their faith. One day he was sitting in one of their assemblies, and the surah (wa'l-Najm idha hawa) [al-Najm: 1] had been revealed to him, so he began to recite it to them until he reached his saying: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [al-Najm: 19–20]. That wish was in his soul, so there flowed upon his tongue what Satan had cast upon him: "Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for." When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went on with his recitation until he finished the surah. When he prostrated at its end, all those in the assembly, Muslims and polytheists, prostrated with him. Then Quraysh dispersed, delighted with that, saying: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods with the best mention." Then Jibril came to him and said: "What have you done? You recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved and feared a great fear, so Allah revealed this verse. Thus they said.

None of this is authentic, nor is it established by any means, and with its lack of authenticity, indeed its falsehood, the verifiers have refuted it by the Book of Allah, the Exalted. Allah says: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–46]. (p-970) And His saying: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3], and His saying: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. Thus He negated even the approach to inclination, let alone inclination.

Al-Bazzar said: this is a report we do not know to be narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) with a connected chain.

Al-Bayhaqi said: this story is not established in terms of transmission; then he began to speak about the narrators of this story being criticized.

Imam al-A'immah Ibn Khuzaymah said: this story is a fabrication of the zanadiqah (heretics).

Qadi Iyad said in al-Shifa': the Community has unanimously agreed that in matters concerning conveyance, he is protected from reporting anything contrary to what he is, neither intentionally, nor deliberately, nor by forgetfulness, nor by error.

Ibn Kathir said: many exegetes have mentioned here the story of the cranes, and of the return of many of the emigrants to the land of Abyssinia, thinking that the polytheists of Quraysh had embraced Islam. But all its routes are mursal (broken in the chain), and I have not seen it transmitted with a connected chain from any sound path.

When the falsehood of that has been established for you, you know that the meaning of tamanna is recited and read, as we have mentioned from al-Wahidi's report on that from the exegetes.

Likewise al-Baghawi said: most exegetes said the meaning of tamanna is recited and read the Book of Allah, and the meaning of ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ is into his recitation and reading.

Ibn Jarir said: this view is closer to the interpretation of the speech, and what preceded in the explanation of His saying: ﴿They know not the Book except wishful thinking (amani)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 78] supports this. It has also been said: the meaning of tamanna is "spoke," and the meaning of ﴿Satan cast into his desire﴾ is into his speech; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. And it has been said: the meaning of tamanna is "said."

The summary of the meaning of the verse: Satan put that into the ears of the polytheists without the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaking it, nor it running upon his tongue. So this verse is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning: let that not terrify you nor grieve you, for the like of this has befallen those before you among the messengers and prophets. And on the assumption that the meaning of tamanna is "he spoke to himself," as related by al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i, for both said: "tamanna" means when he speaks to himself, then the meaning is: when he speaks to himself with something, Satan speaks it and casts it into the ears of the people, without the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaking it or it running upon his tongue.

Ibn Atiyyah said: there is no disagreement that Satan's casting is only into audible words by which the trial occurs.

It has been said concerning the interpretation of the verse: the intended "cranes" are the angels, and this is refuted by His saying: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾, i.e., nullifies it, and the intercession of the angels is not false.

It has been said: that ran upon his tongue (ﷺ) through forgetfulness and oblivion, and both are permissible for the prophets; but it is refuted by the fact that forgetfulness and oblivion are not permissible in matters concerning conveyance, as is established in its proper places. Then, when Allah the Exalted consoled him with this consolation, and that it had befallen those before him among the messengers and prophets, He made clear that He nullifies that and does not confirm it, nor does Satan's deception with it persist. So He said: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾, i.e., nullifies it and makes it passing and not established, ﴿then Allah makes His verses firm﴾, i.e., establishes them, ﴿and Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾, i.e., abundant in knowledge and wisdom in all His sayings and deeds.

The clause ﴿that He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾ is for causation, i.e., that casting which Satan casts is a trial, i.e., misguidance, ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, i.e., doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿and the hard-hearted﴾ are the polytheists, for their hearts never soften to the truth, nor do they return to the right by any means. Then He, the Exalted, recorded against these two groups, those in whose hearts is a disease and those in whose hearts is hardness, that they are wrongdoers, so He said: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾, i.e., severe enmity. Describing the dissension as "far" is an intensification, and the one truly described by it is the one who holds it.

When He, the Exalted, made clear that this casting was a trial regarding the people of hypocrisy, doubt and polytheism, He made clear that for the believers who know Allah and recognize Him, it is a cause for them to attain knowledge that the Qur'an is truth and right. So He said: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾, i.e., the truth sent down from Him. It has been said that the pronoun in "that it" refers to Allah's empowering Satan to cast; because that is among the practices of His prophets. But this is refuted by His saying: ﴿so that they believe in it﴾, for the intended meaning of faith in the Qur'an is that they remain steadfast in faith in it, ﴿and their hearts humble themselves to it﴾, i.e., submit, are humbled and yield; for faith in it and the humbling of hearts to it cannot be an empowerment from Satan, but rather to the Qur'an. ﴿And indeed Allah is the guide of those who believe﴾ in the matters of their religion ﴿to a straight path﴾, i.e., a sound way with no crookedness.

Abu Haywah read (wa-inna Allaha li-hadin alladhina amanu) with tanwin.

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾, i.e., in doubt about the Qur'an. It has been said: about the religion, which the mention of the straight path indicates. It has been said: about Satan's casting, so they say: "Why did he mention the idols favorably and then retract that?" Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read (fi muriyah) with a damma on the mim. ﴿Until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., the Resurrection unexpectedly, suddenly, ﴿or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day﴾, and it is the Day of Resurrection, for there is no day after it, so on this account it is called barren. In the language, "barren" (aqim) is one who has no child; and since days follow one another, that was made like the condition of birth; and since no day comes after that day, it is described as barren. It has been said: it is a day of battle in which they are killed, like the day of Badr. It has been said: the day is described as barren because there is no compassion or mercy in it, so it is as if barren of good. From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 41], i.e., one in which there is no good and which brings no rain.

﴿The dominion on that day is for Allah﴾, i.e., the absolute sovereignty and complete control: on the Day of Resurrection, it belongs to Allah alone, with none contesting Him in it and none repelling Him from it. The clause ﴿He will judge between them﴾ is a resumed sentence answering an implied question. Then He explained this judgment with His saying: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss﴾, i.e., they will dwell in them, settled in their lands, immersed in their delights.

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾, i.e., they combined disbelief in Allah with denial of His signs, ﴿for them is a humiliating punishment﴾, i.e., a punishment characterized as humiliating to those punished, reaching them to the greatest degree.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf the like of it, (p-971) and added: "then muhaddath was abrogated." He said: the muhaddathun are the companion of Ya-Sin, Luqman, the believer of Pharaoh's family, and the companion of Musa.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 58–66 (part 1 of 2):

He, glorified is He, singled out the emigrants for mention, specifying them for greater honour, and said: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾. Some of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: they are those who emigrated from Makkah to Madinah. Others said: those who emigrated from their homelands in a military detachment (sariyyah) or an army. It is not far-fetched to apply it to both, and all of it is in the way of Allah. ﴿Then they were killed or they died﴾, meaning while in the state of emigration. The lam in ﴿Surely Allah will provide for them a goodly provision﴾ is the answer to an implied oath (qasam mahdhuf), and the clause is the predicate (khabar) of the relative pronoun (al-ladhina), with the implied verb of saying (taqdir al-qawl). The word rizqan (a provision) is in the accusative either as a second object, meaning "provided with a goodly provision," or as an emphatic verbal noun (masdar mu'akkidah). The goodly provision is the bliss of Paradise, which does not end. It has been said that it is spoils of war, because it is lawful, and it has been said that it is knowledge and understanding, like the words of Shu'ayb: ﴿and He has provided me from Him with a goodly provision﴾ [Hud: 88].

Ibn 'Amir and the people of Syria read ﴿qutthilu﴾ (thumma qutthilu) with the doubled letter (tashdid), indicating intensification, while the rest read it with a single letter (takhfif). ﴿And surely Allah is the best of providers﴾, for He provides without reckoning. Every provision that comes through the hands of servants to one another is from Him, glorified is He. There is no provider other than Him and no giver besides Him. This clause is a concluding appendix (tadhyil) confirming what precedes it.

The clause ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance which they will be pleased with﴾ is either a new sentence (mustaʼnafah) or a substitute (badal) for the clause ﴿Allah will surely provide for them﴾.

The people of Madinah read ﴿madkhalan﴾ with an open mim, while the rest read it with a damma. It is a noun of place (ism makan) intended to mean Paradise. Its accusative is either as a second object or as a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi) emphasizing the verb mentioned. The discussion of such a construction has already passed in the surah of al-Isra' (Surah Subhan).

In this there is a favour to them and good news for them beyond measure, for the entrance they are pleased with is the most suited to their souls and the closest to their aim. Moreover, they will see in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. That is what they are pleased with, and it is beyond pleasure. ﴿And surely Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the degrees of those who act and the ranks of their deserving, ﴿Most Forbearing﴾ toward the negligence of those among them who are negligent; He does not hasten to punish them. The demonstrative in His words ﴿that﴾ refers to what has preceded.

Al-Zajjaj said: The matter is what We have related to you of the fulfilment of the promise to the emigrants specifically, if they are killed or die. On this view, it is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf).

The meaning of ﴿Whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾ is: whoever repays the wrongdoer with the like of what he wronged him. The beginning of the act is named by the name of the recompense, as a rhetorical device called musha-kalah (naming something by the name of what is associated with it), like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and His words, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾. (p-972) Punishment (ʻuqubah) in its origin occurs only after an act, of which it is the recompense. The meaning of likeness is that he limited himself to the measure by which he was wronged and did not exceed it. The meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the wrongdoer, from the beginning, attacked him again with the injustice after that first injustice. It has been said that the intended oppression here is what the polytheists did in driving the Muslims out of their homelands after they had denied their Prophet and harmed those who believed in him. The lam in ﴿Allah will surely help him﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, meaning: Allah will surely help the one who was oppressed against the oppressor. ﴿Surely Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving﴾, meaning abundantly pardoning and forgiving the believers for whatever sins they committed.

It has also been said: the pardon and forgiveness are for what the believers did in preferring retaliation over pardon. It has been said too that the meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the one who repays was himself oppressed, that is, wronged, and the meaning of "then" (thumma) is a difference in rank, since beginning the fighting with him is a kind of injustice, as is said in the proverbs of the Arabs: "The one who starts is the greater wrongdoer."

It has been said that this verse is Madani and concerns retaliation (qisas) and wounds.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾ refers to what has preceded of Allah's help for the one who was oppressed. It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the clause "because Allah causes to enter," and the ba' is causal, meaning: that is by reason that He, glorified is He, is able. From the perfection of His power is the causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night. He expressed the increase of one by "entering" because the increase of one entails the decrease of the other. The intended meaning is the establishment of one of the two attributes in the place of the other.

The meaning of this entering was discussed earlier in Surah Al 'Imran. ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears everything heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, who sees everything seen; or, He hears the sayings and sees the deeds, so nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ refers to what has preceded of His being described with the perfection of overpowering power and complete knowledge. That is, He, glorified is He, is the possessor of truth, so His religion is true, His worship is true, His help for His allies against their enemies is true, and His promise is true. He, mighty and majestic, in His essence, His acts, and His attributes, is the Truth. ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Shu'bah read ﴿tad'una﴾ with the second-person (ta') addressing the polytheists, and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. The rest read it with the third-person (ya') as a report, and Abu 'Ubaydah preferred this reading.

The meaning is: those you call upon as gods, which are idols, are the falsehood that has no establishment, neither in itself nor in being gods. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾, meaning exalted over everything by His power, sanctified above equals and rivals, free of the attributes that the wrongdoers ascribe to Him, ﴿the Great﴾, that is, possessor of greatness. This refers to the perfection of His essence and His singularity in divinity.

Then He, glorified is He, cited a clear proof of His perfect power, saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ The interrogation is for affirmation (istifham al-taqrir), and the fa' is for conjunction with "sent down." The verb after the fa' is in the nominative because, as an interrogation of affirmation, it has the status of a declarative statement, as al-Khalil and Sibawayh said.

Al-Khalil said: The meaning is "He sent down water from the sky, and so it was thus and thus," as the poet said:

"Did you not ask the desolate campsite, and it spoke? Or will the barren plain (sumlaq) tell you today?"

Its meaning is: you have asked it, and it spoke. Al-Farra' said: "Have you not seen" is a report, just as you say in speech: "Indeed Allah sends down water from the sky, and so the earth becomes green," that is, possessing greenness, just as you say "mubqilah" (possessing herbage) and "musbi'ah" (possessing wild beasts). The present-tense form expresses the earth's rapid greening after the descent of water with vegetation, and its continuing in this way habitually. The form of the future is to bring the image of greening to mind, with an indication of the renewal and continuation of the sending down. This meaning is achieved only by the present tense, and the nominative is definite here, because if it were in the accusative, the intended meaning of the verse would be reversed, turning into a negation of greening, whereas what is intended is its affirmation.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This does not happen, meaning greening in the morning after a night of rain, except in Makkah and Tihamah.

The apparent meaning of greening is the greening of the earth itself, not with respect to the vegetation in it, as in His words: ﴿So when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ [Fussilat: 39]. The intended meaning of His words ﴿Surely Allah is Subtle﴾ is that His knowledge reaches every fine and great thing. It has been said: Subtle regarding the provisions of His servants. It has been said: Subtle in bringing forth vegetation. The meaning of ﴿All-Aware﴾ is that He has expertise in managing His servants and what suits them. It has been said: All-Aware of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed. It has been said: All-Aware of their need and destitution.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾, in creation, ownership and disposal, and all of them are in need of His provision. ﴿And surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient﴾, so He needs nothing. ﴿The Praiseworthy﴾ is the one deserving praise in every state.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected for you what is in the earth﴾. This is another blessing that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. He informed His servants that He subjected for them what they need, from animals, trees and rivers, and made it for their benefits. "The ship" (al-fulk) is conjoined either to "what" or to the subject of "inna," meaning: and He subjected to you the ship while it runs in the sea. 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read ﴿wal-fulku﴾ with a damma as the subject, and what follows it as its predicate, while the rest read it in the accusative.

The meaning of ﴿running upon the sea by His command﴾ is by His decree. The clause is in the place of an accusative of circumstance (hal) according to the reading of the majority. ﴿And He withholds the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, meaning lest it fall, and this is because He created it with a quality that entails its being held up. The clause is conjoined to "runs." ﴿Except by His permission﴾, meaning by His will and His wish, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Surely Allah is to people Compassionate, Merciful﴾, meaning abundantly full of tenderness and mercy, in that He subjected these matters to His servants and prepared for them the means of livelihood, and He withheld the sky from falling upon the earth and destroying them, as a bounty from Him to His servants and a favour upon them.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned another blessing, saying: ﴿And He is the One who gave you life﴾ after you had been lifeless matter, ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ at the end of your lifespans, ﴿then He will give you life﴾ at the resurrection for reckoning and punishment. ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, meaning abundantly ungrateful for the blessings of Allah upon him, even though they are manifest and not hidden. They passed by two funerals, one of a slain man and the other of one who died naturally. The people turned away from the slain one. Fadalah said: "Why do I see the people turning from this and leaving that?" They said: "This one was slain in the way of Allah." I say: This is supported by the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muqatil, concerning His words: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾, that he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) sent a detachment during two nights that remained of Muharram, and they met the polytheists. The polytheists said to one another: 'Fight the companions of Muhammad, for they consider fighting in the sacred month unlawful.' The companions of Muhammad appealed to them and reminded them of Allah, asking them not to engage them in battle, for they do not permit fighting in the sacred month except against one who initiates it. The polytheists then initiated the attack and fought them, so the Companions then made fighting them lawful, and they fought them, and Allah gave them victory over them." This is a mursal (a report lacking the Companion's link).

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words: ﴿And whoever retaliates﴾, the verse, that he said: "The polytheists cooperated against the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and drove him out, so Allah promised him that He would help him." This also concerns retaliation.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾, that he said: "Shaytan (Satan)."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 58–66 (part 1 of 2):

Some of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: they are those who emigrated from Makkah to Madinah. Others said: those who emigrated from their homelands in a military detachment (sariyyah) or an army. It is not far-fetched to apply it to both, and all of it is in the way of Allah. ﴿Then they were killed or they died﴾, meaning while in the state of emigration. The lam in ﴿Surely Allah will provide for them a goodly provision﴾ is the answer to an implied oath (qasam mahdhuf), and the clause is the predicate (khabar) of the relative pronoun (al-ladhina), with the implied verb of saying (taqdir al-qawl). The word rizqan (a provision) is in the accusative either as a second object, meaning "provided with a goodly provision," or as an emphatic verbal noun (masdar mu'akkidah). The goodly provision is the bliss of Paradise, which does not end. It has been said that it is spoils of war, because it is lawful, and it has been said that it is knowledge and understanding, like the words of Shu'ayb: ﴿and He has provided me from Him with a goodly provision﴾ [Hud: 88].

Ibn 'Amir and the people of Syria read ﴿qutthilu﴾ (thumma qutthilu) with the doubled letter (tashdid), indicating intensification, while the rest read it with a single letter (takhfif). ﴿And surely Allah is the best of providers﴾, for He provides without reckoning. Every provision that comes through the hands of servants to one another is from Him, glorified is He. There is no provider other than Him and no giver besides Him. This clause is a concluding appendix (tadhyil) confirming what precedes it.

The clause ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance which they will be pleased with﴾ is either a new sentence (mustaʼnafah) or a substitute (badal) for the clause ﴿Allah will surely provide for them﴾.

The people of Madinah read ﴿madkhalan﴾ with an open mim, while the rest read it with a damma. It is a noun of place (ism makan) intended to mean Paradise. Its accusative is either as a second object or as a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi) emphasizing the verb mentioned. The discussion of such a construction has already passed in the surah of al-Isra' (Surah Subhan).

In this there is a favour to them and good news for them beyond measure, for the entrance they are pleased with is the most suited to their souls and the closest to their aim. Moreover, they will see in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. That is what they are pleased with, and it is beyond pleasure. ﴿And surely Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the degrees of those who act and the ranks of their deserving, ﴿Most Forbearing﴾ toward the negligence of those among them who are negligent; He does not hasten to punish them. The demonstrative in His words ﴿that﴾ refers to what has preceded.

Al-Zajjaj said: The matter is what We have related to you of the fulfilment of the promise to the emigrants specifically, if they are killed or die. On this view, it is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf).

The meaning of ﴿Whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾ is: whoever repays the wrongdoer with the like of what he wronged him. The beginning of the act is named by the name of the recompense, as a rhetorical device called musha-kalah (naming something by the name of what is associated with it), like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and His words, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾. (p-972) Punishment (ʻuqubah) in its origin occurs only after an act, of which it is the recompense. The meaning of likeness is that he limited himself to the measure by which he was wronged and did not exceed it. The meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the wrongdoer, from the beginning, attacked him again with the injustice after that first injustice. It has been said that the intended oppression here is what the polytheists did in driving the Muslims out of their homelands after they had denied their Prophet and harmed those who believed in him. The lam in ﴿Allah will surely help him﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, meaning: Allah will surely help the one who was oppressed against the oppressor. ﴿Surely Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving﴾, meaning abundantly pardoning and forgiving the believers for whatever sins they committed.

It has also been said: the pardon and forgiveness are for what the believers did in preferring retaliation over pardon. It has been said too that the meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the one who repays was himself oppressed, that is, wronged, and the meaning of "then" (thumma) is a difference in rank, since beginning the fighting with him is a kind of injustice, as is said in the proverbs of the Arabs: "The one who starts is the greater wrongdoer."

It has been said that this verse is Madani and concerns retaliation (qisas) and wounds.

It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the clause "because Allah causes to enter," and the ba' is causal, meaning: that is by reason that He, glorified is He, is able. From the perfection of His power is the causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night. He expressed the increase of one by "entering" because the increase of one entails the decrease of the other. The intended meaning is the establishment of one of the two attributes in the place of the other.

The meaning of this entering was discussed earlier in Surah Al 'Imran. ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears everything heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, who sees everything seen; or, He hears the sayings and sees the deeds, so nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ refers to what has preceded of His being described with the perfection of overpowering power and complete knowledge. That is, He, glorified is He, is the possessor of truth, so His religion is true, His worship is true, His help for His allies against their enemies is true, and His promise is true. The meaning is: those you call upon as gods, which are idols, are the falsehood that has no establishment, neither in itself nor in being gods. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾, meaning exalted over everything by His power, sanctified above equals and rivals, free of the attributes that the wrongdoers ascribe to Him, ﴿the Great﴾, that is, possessor of greatness. This refers to the perfection of His essence and His singularity in divinity.

It has been said: Subtle in bringing forth vegetation. The meaning of ﴿All-Aware﴾ is that He has expertise in managing His servants and what suits them. It has been said: All-Aware of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed. It has been said: All-Aware of their need and destitution.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾, in creation, ownership and disposal, and all of them are in need of His provision. ﴿And surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient﴾, so He needs nothing. ﴿The Praiseworthy﴾ is the one deserving praise in every state.

He informed His servants that He subjected for them what they need, from animals, trees and rivers, and made it for their benefits. This refers to the perfection of His essence and His singularity in divinity.

It has been said: All-Aware of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed. It has been said: All-Aware of their need and destitution.

It has been said too that the meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the one who repays was himself oppressed, that is, wronged, and the meaning of "then" (thumma) is a difference in rank, since beginning the fighting with him is a kind of injustice, as is said in the proverbs of the Arabs: "The one who starts is the greater wrongdoer."

It has been said that this verse is Madani and concerns retaliation (qisas) and wounds.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾ refers to what has preceded of Allah's help for the one who was oppressed. It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the clause "because Allah causes to enter," and the ba' is causal, meaning: that is by reason that He, glorified is He, is able. From the perfection of His power is the causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night. He expressed the increase of one by "entering" because the increase of one entails the decrease of the other. The intended meaning is the establishment of one of the two attributes in the place of the other.

The meaning of this entering was discussed earlier in Surah Al 'Imran. ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears everything heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, who sees everything seen; or, He hears the sayings and sees the deeds, so nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ refers to what has preceded of His being described with the perfection of overpowering power and complete knowledge. That is, He, glorified is He, is the possessor of truth, so His religion is true, His worship is true, His help for His allies against their enemies is true, and His promise is true. He, mighty and majestic, in His essence, His acts, and His attributes, is the Truth. ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Shu'bah read ﴿tad'una﴾ with the second-person (ta') addressing the polytheists, and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. The rest read it with the third-person (ya') as a report, and Abu 'Ubaydah preferred this reading.

The meaning is: those you call upon as gods, which are idols, are the falsehood that has no establishment, neither in itself nor in being gods. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾, meaning exalted over everything by His power, sanctified above equals and rivals, free of the attributes that the wrongdoers ascribe to Him, ﴿the Great﴾, that is, possessor of greatness. This refers to the perfection of His essence and His singularity in divinity.

"Did you not ask the desolate campsite, and it spoke? Or will the barren plain (sumlaq) tell you today?"

The present-tense form expresses the earth's rapid greening after the descent of water with vegetation, and its continuing in this way habitually. The form of the future is to bring the image of greening to mind, with an indication of the renewal and continuation of the sending down. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This does not happen, meaning greening in the morning after a night of rain, except in Makkah and Tihamah.

It has been said: All-Aware of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed. It has been said: All-Aware of their need and destitution.

He informed His servants that He subjected for them what they need, from animals, trees and rivers, and made it for their benefits. 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read ﴿wal-fulku﴾ with a damma as the subject, and what follows it as its predicate, while the rest read it in the accusative.

The clause is in the place of an accusative of circumstance (hal) according to the reading of the majority. ﴿And He withholds the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, meaning lest it fall, and this is because He created it with a quality that entails its being held up. That is what they are pleased with, and it is beyond pleasure. ﴿And surely Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the degrees of those who act and the ranks of their deserving, ﴿Most Forbearing﴾ toward the negligence of those among them who are negligent; He does not hasten to punish them. The demonstrative in His words ﴿that﴾ refers to what has preceded.

Al-Zajjaj said: The matter is what We have related to you of the fulfilment of the promise to the emigrants specifically, if they are killed or die. On this view, it is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf).

The meaning of ﴿Whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾ is: whoever repays the wrongdoer with the like of what he wronged him. The beginning of the act is named by the name of the recompense, as a rhetorical device called musha-kalah (naming something by the name of what is associated with it), like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and His words, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾. (p-972) Punishment (ʻuqubah) in its origin occurs only after an act, of which it is the recompense. The meaning of likeness is that he limited himself to the measure by which he was wronged and did not exceed it. The meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the wrongdoer, from the beginning, attacked him again with the injustice after that first injustice. It has been said that the intended oppression here is what the polytheists did in driving the Muslims out of their homelands after they had denied their Prophet and harmed those who believed in him. The lam in ﴿Allah will surely help him﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, meaning: Allah will surely help the one who was oppressed against the oppressor. ﴿Surely Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving﴾, meaning abundantly pardoning and forgiving the believers for whatever sins they committed.

It has also been said: the pardon and forgiveness are for what the believers did in preferring retaliation over pardon. It has been said too that the meaning of ﴿then he is oppressed﴾ is that the one who repays was himself oppressed, that is, wronged, and the meaning of "then" (thumma) is a difference in rank, since beginning the fighting with him is a kind of injustice, as is said in the proverbs of the Arabs: "The one who starts is the greater wrongdoer."

It has been said that this verse is Madani and concerns retaliation (qisas) and wounds.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾ refers to what has preceded of Allah's help for the one who was oppressed. It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the clause "because Allah causes to enter," and the ba' is causal, meaning: that is by reason that He, glorified is He, is able. From the perfection of His power is the causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night. He expressed the increase of one by "entering" because the increase of one entails the decrease of the other. The intended meaning is the establishment of one of the two attributes in the place of the other.

The meaning of this entering was discussed earlier in Surah Al 'Imran. ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears everything heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, who sees everything seen; or, He hears the sayings and sees the deeds, so nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ refers to what has preceded of His being described with the perfection of overpowering power and complete knowledge. That is, He, glorified is He, is the possessor of truth, so His religion is true, His worship is true, His help for His allies against their enemies is true, and His promise is true. He, mighty and majestic, in His essence, His acts, and His attributes, is the Truth. ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Shu'bah read ﴿tad'una﴾ with the second-person (ta') addressing the polytheists, and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. The rest read it with the third-person (ya') as a report, and Abu 'Ubaydah preferred this reading.

The meaning is: those you call upon as gods, which are idols, are the falsehood that has no establishment, neither in itself nor in being gods. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾, meaning exalted over everything by His power, sanctified above equals and rivals, free of the attributes that the wrongdoers ascribe to Him, ﴿the Great﴾, that is, possessor of greatness. This refers to the perfection of His essence and His singularity in divinity.

Then He, glorified is He, cited a clear proof of His perfect power, saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ The interrogation is for affirmation (istifham al-taqrir), and the fa' is for conjunction with "sent down." The verb after the fa' is in the nominative because, as an interrogation of affirmation, it has the status of a declarative statement, as al-Khalil and Sibawayh said.

Al-Khalil said: The meaning is "He sent down water from the sky, and so it was thus and thus," as the poet said:

"Did you not ask the desolate campsite, and it spoke? Or will the barren plain (sumlaq) tell you today?"

Its meaning is: you have asked it, and it spoke. Al-Farra' said: "Have you not seen" is a report, just as you say in speech: "Indeed Allah sends down water from the sky, and so the earth becomes green," that is, possessing greenness, just as you say "mubqilah" (possessing herbage) and "musbi'ah" (possessing wild beasts). The present-tense form expresses the earth's rapid greening after the descent of water with vegetation, and its continuing in this way habitually. The form of the future is to bring the image of greening to mind, with an indication of the renewal and continuation of the sending down. This meaning is achieved only by the present tense, and the nominative is definite here, because if it were in the accusative, the intended meaning of the verse would be reversed, turning into a negation of greening, whereas what is intended is its affirmation.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This does not happen, meaning greening in the morning after a night of rain, except in Makkah and Tihamah.

The apparent meaning of greening is the greening of the earth itself, not with respect to the vegetation in it, as in His words: ﴿So when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ [Fussilat: 39]. The intended meaning of His words ﴿Surely Allah is Subtle﴾ is that His knowledge reaches every fine and great thing. It has been said: Subtle regarding the provisions of His servants. It has been said: Subtle in bringing forth vegetation. The meaning of ﴿All-Aware﴾ is that He has expertise in managing His servants and what suits them. It has been said: All-Aware of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed. It has been said: All-Aware of their need and destitution.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾, in creation, ownership and disposal, and all of them are in need of His provision. ﴿And surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient﴾, so He needs nothing. ﴿The Praiseworthy﴾ is the one deserving praise in every state.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected for you what is in the earth﴾. This is another blessing that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. He informed His servants that He subjected for them what they need, from animals, trees and rivers, and made it for their benefits. "The ship" (al-fulk) is conjoined either to "what" or to the subject of "inna," meaning: and He subjected to you the ship while it runs in the sea. 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read ﴿wal-fulku﴾ with a damma as the subject, and what follows it as its predicate, while the rest read it in the accusative.

The meaning of ﴿running upon the sea by His command﴾ is by His decree. The clause is in the place of an accusative of circumstance (hal) according to the reading of the majority. ﴿And He withholds the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, meaning lest it fall, and this is because He created it with a quality that entails its being held up. The clause is conjoined to "runs." ﴿Except by His permission﴾, meaning by His will and His wish, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Surely Allah is to people Compassionate, Merciful﴾, meaning abundantly full of tenderness and mercy, in that He subjected these matters to His servants and prepared for them the means of livelihood, and He withheld the sky from falling upon the earth and destroying them, as a bounty from Him to His servants and a favour upon them.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned another blessing, saying: ﴿And He is the One who gave you life﴾ after you had been lifeless matter, ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ at the end of your lifespans, ﴿then He will give you life﴾ at the resurrection for reckoning and punishment. ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, meaning abundantly ungrateful for the blessings of Allah upon him, even though they are manifest and not hidden. This does not contradict the exception of some individuals from this ingratitude, because what is meant is describing the whole category with the attribute of those among its members in whom it is found, for emphasis.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Salman al-Farisi: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever dies while stationed in frontier defence (murabitan), Allah will continue for him the same reward, will continue his provision for him, and he will be safe from the tempters (al-fattanin). Recite, if you wish: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah, then were killed or died﴾ (p-973) up to His words: ﴿Forbearing﴾."

The chain of Ibn Abi Hatim is as follows: Al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Uqbah, that is Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Uqbah, who said: Shurahbil ibn al-Simt said: Our frontier garrison and our stay at a fortress in the land of the Romans lasted long, and Salman passed by me, that is al-Farisi, and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd al-Ansari, the Companion, that he was at Rhodes (Rudus). They passed by two funerals, one of a slain man and the other of one who died naturally. The people turned away from the slain one. Fadalah said: "Why do I see the people turning from this and leaving that?" They said: "This one was slain in the way of Allah." He said: "By Allah, I do not care in which of the two graves I am raised. Listen to the Book of Allah: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah, then were killed or died﴾," the verse.

Its chain according to Ibn Abi Hatim is as follows: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us from Zayd ibn Bishr, Dimam informed me that he heard Abu Qubayl and Rabi'ah ibn Sayf al-Mu'afiri say: "We were at Rhodes, and with us was Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd al-Ansari, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," and he mentioned it.

I say: This is supported by the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muqatil, concerning His words: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾, that he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) sent a detachment during two nights that remained of Muharram, and they met the polytheists. The polytheists said to one another: 'Fight the companions of Muhammad, for they consider fighting in the sacred month unlawful.' The companions of Muhammad appealed to them and reminded them of Allah, asking them not to engage them in battle, for they do not permit fighting in the sacred month except against one who initiates it. The polytheists then initiated the attack and fought them, so the Companions then made fighting them lawful, and they fought them, and Allah gave them victory over them." This is a mursal (a report lacking the Companion's link).

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words: ﴿And whoever retaliates﴾, the verse, that he said: "The polytheists cooperated against the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and drove him out, so Allah promised him that He would help him." This also concerns retaliation.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 58–66 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾, that he said: "Shaytan (Satan)."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan regarding His words ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾, that he said: "He counts the calamities and forgets the blessings."

He (glorified is He) returned to explaining the matter of the religious obligations, with a rebuke to the people of the earlier religions contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for disputing with him. He said: ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾, meaning: for every one of the past generations We set a specific law, such that no community among them would go beyond its own prescribed law to another. The clause ﴿they are its performers﴾ is a description of "mansak," and the pronoun refers to "every community." That is, that community is the one that acts upon it, and no other. So the Torah was the rite of the community that existed from the mission of Musa (Moses) to the mission of Isa (Jesus), the Gospel was the rite of the community that existed from the mission of Isa to the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the Qur'an is the rite of the Muslims. "Mansak" is a verbal noun (masdar), not a noun of place, as the phrase "they are its performers" indicates; he did not say "performers in it."

It was said: "mansak" means the place where worship is performed. It was also said: it means the sacrificial slaughter. There is no basis for restricting it in this way, and no consideration is given to the specific occasion of revelation.

The fa' in His words ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ is for the consequence of the prohibition on what precedes it. The pronoun refers to the nations whose traces remain, that is: We have specified for every community a law, and this Muhammadan community is among those nations. This necessitates that those among them who remain should not dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it entails that they obey him in matters of religion. The prohibition is either on its literal meaning, or it is a metaphor (kinayah) for forbidding him (ﷺ) from paying attention to their disputing with him.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is a prohibition addressed to him (ﷺ) against disputing with them, that is: do not dispute with them yourself, just as you say, "Let so-and-so not quarrel with you," meaning, "Do not quarrel with him," and just as you say, "Let so-and-so not strike you," meaning, "Do not strike him." This is because the form of mufa'alah (reciprocal action) implicitly requires the reverse, and it is not permissible to say "Let so-and-so not strike you" while meaning "Do not strike him."

It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said regarding the meaning of the verse: ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾, that is: let them not argue with you. He said: What indicates this is ﴿And if they argue with you﴾. Abu Mijlaz recited "fa-la yanza'unnaka fi al-amr" (let them not draw you away in the matter), meaning: let them not make you light-headed, nor overpower you in your religion.

The rest of the readers recited "yunazi'unnaka" from disputing (al-munazi'ah). ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, that is: call these disputers, or call people in general, to the religion of Allah, His unity, and belief in Him. ﴿Indeed, you are upon a straight guidance﴾, that is, a straight path with no crookedness in it.

﴿And if they argue with you﴾, that is: and if they refuse anything but argument after the clarification and the manifestation of the proof against them, ﴿then say: Allah knows best what you do﴾, that is: entrust their affair to Allah, and say to them this statement which includes a threat.

﴿Allah will judge between you﴾, that is, between the Muslims and the disbelievers, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, whereupon the truth will be distinguished from falsehood. In this verse there is instruction for this community on what they should answer to whoever wants to argue with falsehood. It was also said that it has been abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

The sentence ﴿Do you not know﴾ is resumed (mustanafah), confirming the content of what precedes it, and the interrogative is for affirmation: that is, you have known, O Muhammad, and you are certain, that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and among that is what you differ about. Indeed, that which is in the heaven and the earth is among His knowledge, in a Book, that is, written with Him in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab). ﴿Indeed, that is upon Allah easy﴾, that is: indeed the judgment from Him, glorified is He, between His servants concerning what they differ about is easy for Him, not difficult; or the encompassing of His knowledge of what is in the heaven and the earth is easy for Him.

﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [p. 974]. This is a recounting of some of their shameful acts, that is: they worship idols for which they have not held to any clear proof from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿And that about which they have no knowledge﴾, that is, from any rational proof indicating the permissibility of that in any way. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾, one who would help them and repel from them the punishment of Allah. The discussion of this verse has already preceded in Surat Al 'Imran.

The clause ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, clear﴾ is conjoined to "they worship," and "clear" (bayyinat) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), that is: in the state of being plain, manifest in their indication. ﴿You recognize in the faces of those who disbelieved the denial﴾, that is, the matter that is denied, which is their anger and frowning when they hear it; or the meaning of "al-munkar" is the act of denial, that is: you recognize in their faces their rejection of it. It was said that it is arrogance and haughtiness. The clause ﴿they almost assault those who recite to them Our verses﴾ is resumed, being an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: what is that denial which is recognized in their faces? So it was answered: "they almost assault," that is, they strike out. "Al-satwah" is the intensity of striking; one says "sata bihi yasutu" when he strikes him with a blow, or an insult, or by seizing him with the hand. The origin of "al-sat'" is subjugation.

Thus you see the people of misguided innovations: when one of them hears what the scholar recites to them of the verses of the Mighty Book, or of the sound Sunnah, opposing what he believes of falsehood and error, you see in his face such denial that, if he were able to assault that scholar, he would do to him what he does not do even to the polytheists. We have seen and heard from the people of innovation what description cannot encompass. And Allah is the Helper of the truth, the Manifester of the religion, the Refuter of falsehood, the Crusher of innovations, and the Guardian of those who speak, by what He has taken from them, those who make clear to people what has been sent down to them. He is our sufficiency and the best Disposer of affairs.

Then He commanded His Messenger to respond to them, saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾, that is: shall I inform you of ﴿that which is worse than that which is in you﴾, namely the rage you feel against those who recite to you the verses of Allah, and your readiness to pounce upon them. It is ﴿the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. So "the Fire" is in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: what is this matter which is worse than what we endure and struggle with when we hear what you recite to us? So he said: it is ﴿the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. It was also said that "the Fire" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is the clause ﴿which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. It was also said that the meaning is: shall I inform you of something worse than what befalls the reciter of the Qur'an from you, of harm, threats against them, and pouncing upon them? "The Fire" was also read in the accusative, with the implied sense "I mean," and it was read in the genitive as a substitute (badal) for "worse." ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place to which you will return, which is the Fire.

It has been related by Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They are its performers﴾, that he said: it means they are its slaughterers. ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾, meaning in the matter of slaughtering. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid something similar as well.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid, who said: ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ is the saying of the people of polytheism: "What Allah has slaughtered with His right hand, do not eat it; but what you slaughter with your own hands is lawful."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah created the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) for a journey of one hundred years, and He said to the Pen, before He created creation, while it was upon the Throne: "Write." It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "My knowledge of My creation until the Day the Hour is established." So the Pen ran with what is to occur in the knowledge of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. That is His saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth﴾, meaning what is in the seven heavens and the seven earths; that this knowledge is in a Book, meaning in the Preserved Tablet, written before He created the heavens and the earths. ﴿Indeed, that is upon Allah easy﴾, meaning: easy.
