It has been related by Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They are its performers﴾, that he said: it means they are its slaughterers. ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾, meaning in the matter of slaughtering. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid something similar as well.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid, who said: ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ is the saying of the people of polytheism: "What Allah has slaughtered with His right hand, do not eat it; but what you slaughter with your own hands is lawful."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah created the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) for a journey of one hundred years, and He said to the Pen, before He created creation, while it was upon the Throne: "Write." It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "My knowledge of My creation until the Day the Hour is established." So the Pen ran with what is to occur in the knowledge of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. That is His saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth﴾, meaning what is in the seven heavens and the seven earths; that this knowledge is in a Book, meaning in the Preserved Tablet, written before He created the heavens and the earths. ﴿Indeed, that is upon Allah easy﴾, meaning: easy.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They almost assault﴾, meaning: they strike out.

He (glorified is He) returned to explaining the matter of the religious obligations, with a rebuke to the people of the earlier religions contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for disputing with him. He said: ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾, meaning: for every one of the past generations We set a specific law, such that no community among them would go beyond its own prescribed law to another. The clause ﴿they are its performers﴾ is a description of "mansak," and the pronoun refers to "every community." That is, that community is the one that acts upon it, and no other. So the Torah was the rite of the community that existed from the mission of Musa (Moses) to the mission of Isa (Jesus), the Gospel was the rite of the community that existed from the mission of Isa to the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the Qur'an is the rite of the Muslims. "Mansak" is a verbal noun (masdar), not a noun of place, as the phrase "they are its performers" indicates; he did not say "performers in it."

It was said: "mansak" means the place where worship is performed. It was also said: it means the sacrificial slaughter. There is no basis for restricting it in this way, and no consideration is given to the specific occasion of revelation.

The fa' in His words ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ is for the consequence of the prohibition on what precedes it. The pronoun refers to the nations whose traces remain, that is: We have specified for every community a law, and this Muhammadan community is among those nations. This necessitates that those among them who remain should not dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it entails that they obey him in matters of religion. The prohibition is either on its literal meaning, or it is a metaphor (kinayah) for forbidding him (ﷺ) from paying attention to their disputing with him.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is a prohibition addressed to him (ﷺ) against disputing with them, that is: do not dispute with them yourself, just as you say, "Let so-and-so not quarrel with you," meaning, "Do not quarrel with him," and just as you say, "Let so-and-so not strike you," meaning, "Do not strike him." This is because the form of mufa'alah (reciprocal action) implicitly requires the reverse, and it is not permissible to say "Let so-and-so not strike you" while meaning "Do not strike him."

It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said regarding the meaning of the verse: ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾, that is: let them not argue with you. He said: What indicates this is ﴿And if they argue with you﴾. Abu Mijlaz recited "fa-la yanza'unnaka fi al-amr" (let them not draw you away in the matter), meaning: let them not make you light-headed, nor overpower you in your religion.

The rest of the readers recited "yunazi'unnaka" from disputing (al-munazi'ah). ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, that is: call these disputers, or call people in general, to the religion of Allah, His unity, and belief in Him. ﴿Indeed, you are upon a straight guidance﴾, that is, a straight path with no crookedness in it.

﴿And if they argue with you﴾, that is: and if they refuse anything but argument after the clarification and the manifestation of the proof against them, ﴿then say: Allah knows best what you do﴾, that is: entrust their affair to Allah, and say to them this statement which includes a threat.

﴿Allah will judge between you﴾, that is, between the Muslims and the disbelievers, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, whereupon the truth will be distinguished from falsehood. In this verse there is instruction for this community on what they should answer to whoever wants to argue with falsehood. It was also said that it has been abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

The sentence ﴿Do you not know﴾ is resumed (mustanafah), confirming the content of what precedes it, and the interrogative is for affirmation: that is, you have known, O Muhammad, and you are certain, that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and among that is what you differ about. Indeed, that which is in the heaven and the earth is among His knowledge, in a Book, that is, written with Him in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab). ﴿Indeed, that is upon Allah easy﴾, that is: indeed the judgment from Him, glorified is He, between His servants concerning what they differ about is easy for Him, not difficult; or the encompassing of His knowledge of what is in the heaven and the earth is easy for Him.

﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [p. 974]. This is a recounting of some of their shameful acts, that is: they worship idols for which they have not held to any clear proof from Allah, glorified is He. ﴿And that about which they have no knowledge﴾, that is, from any rational proof indicating the permissibility of that in any way. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾, one who would help them and repel from them the punishment of Allah. The discussion of this verse has already preceded in Surat Al 'Imran.

The clause ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, clear﴾ is conjoined to "they worship," and "clear" (bayyinat) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), that is: in the state of being plain, manifest in their indication. ﴿You recognize in the faces of those who disbelieved the denial﴾, that is, the matter that is denied, which is their anger and frowning when they hear it; or the meaning of "al-munkar" is the act of denial, that is: you recognize in their faces their rejection of it. It was said that it is arrogance and haughtiness. The clause ﴿they almost assault those who recite to them Our verses﴾ is resumed, being an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: what is that denial which is recognized in their faces? So it was answered: "they almost assault," that is, they strike out. "Al-satwah" is the intensity of striking; one says "sata bihi yasutu" when he strikes him with a blow, or an insult, or by seizing him with the hand. The origin of "al-sat'" is subjugation.

Thus you see the people of misguided innovations: when one of them hears what the scholar recites to them of the verses of the Mighty Book, or of the sound Sunnah, opposing what he believes of falsehood and error, you see in his face such denial that, if he were able to assault that scholar, he would do to him what he does not do even to the polytheists. We have seen and heard from the people of innovation what description cannot encompass. And Allah is the Helper of the truth, the Manifester of the religion, the Refuter of falsehood, the Crusher of innovations, and the Guardian of those who speak, by what He has taken from them, those who make clear to people what has been sent down to them. He is our sufficiency and the best Disposer of affairs.

Then He commanded His Messenger to respond to them, saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾, that is: shall I inform you of ﴿that which is worse than that which is in you﴾, namely the rage you feel against those who recite to you the verses of Allah, and your readiness to pounce upon them. It is ﴿the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. So "the Fire" is in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: what is this matter which is worse than what we endure and struggle with when we hear what you recite to us? So he said: it is ﴿the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. It was also said that "the Fire" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is the clause ﴿which Allah has promised those who disbelieved﴾. It was also said that the meaning is: shall I inform you of something worse than what befalls the reciter of the Qur'an from you, of harm, threats against them, and pouncing upon them? "The Fire" was also read in the accusative, with the implied sense "I mean," and it was read in the genitive as a substitute (badal) for "worse." ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place to which you will return, which is the Fire.

It has been related by Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They are its performers﴾, that he said: it means they are its slaughterers. ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾, meaning in the matter of slaughtering. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid something similar as well.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid, who said: ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ is the saying of the people of polytheism: "What Allah has slaughtered with His right hand, do not eat it; but what you slaughter with your own hands is lawful."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah created the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) for a journey of one hundred years, and He said to the Pen, before He created creation, while it was upon the Throne: "Write." It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "My knowledge of My creation until the Day the Hour is established." So the Pen ran with what is to occur in the knowledge of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. That is His saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth﴾, meaning what is in the seven heavens and the seven earths; that this knowledge is in a Book, meaning in the Preserved Tablet, written before He created the heavens and the earths. ﴿Indeed, that is upon Allah easy﴾, meaning: easy.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They almost assault﴾, meaning: they strike out.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 73–78 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined, so listen to it﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿and they worship, besides Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority﴾. Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, a grammarian) said: "There is no parable here. The meaning is: they coined a parable for Me, so listen to their statement." That is, the disbelievers made for Allah a likeness by worshipping other than Him. It is as if He said: "They made a likeness for Me in My worship, so listen to the account of this likeness."

Al-Qutaybi (al-Qutaybi, a lexicographer) said: "The meaning is: O mankind, the example of those who worship gods that cannot create a fly, and if it snatches something from them, they cannot rescue it from it."

Al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, a grammarian and exegete) said: "The meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, coined a parable for what they worship besides Him." He said: "This is among the best things said about it," i.e., Allah has explained to you a likeness, and to your deity.

The origin of a *mathal* (parable) is a sentence of speech that is received with approval and acceptance, circulated among people and regarded as remarkable. They made its source of coinage a parable for its occasion. Then they may borrow it for a story, a situation, or a quality that is remarkable, because it resembles it in strangeness, like this story mentioned in this verse.

What is meant by ﴿those they call upon besides Allah﴾ is the idols around the Ka'bah and others. It has also been said that it refers to the leaders who turned them away from obedience to Allah, because they were the people who loosed and bound among them. It has also been said that it refers to the devils who led them to disobey Allah. The first is more fitting to the context and clearer in the parable. *Al-dhubab* (the fly) is a noun for the single insect, used for both male and female. Its plural of paucity is *adhibbah*, and its plural of abundance is *dhibban*, like *ghurab* (crow), *aghribah*, and *ghirban*.

Al-Jawhari (al-Jawhari, a lexicographer) said: "*Al-dhubab* is well known; its singular is *dhubabah*." The meaning is: they will not be able to create it, despite its being small in body and insignificant in essence.

The clause ﴿and if they gathered together for it﴾ is conjoined to another conditional clause that is omitted, meaning: "If they did not gather for it, they would not create it, and even if they gathered for it." The response is omitted, and the estimate is: "they will not create it." Both clauses are in the accusative position as a circumstantial state, meaning: they will not create it in any state.

Then He, glorified is He, explained the completeness of their incapacity and the weakness of their power, so He said: ﴿and if the fly snatches from them anything, they cannot rescue it from it﴾. That is, if the fly takes from them anything of things, they are unable to free it from it, because of the completeness of their incapacity and the extreme of their weakness. *Al-istinqadh* and *al-inqadh* mean rescue and deliverance. If they are unable to create this weak creature, and unable to rescue what it took from them, then they are more incapable and weaker regarding something other than it that is greater in body and stronger in power.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the weakness of the idols and the fly, so He said: ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾. The idol is like the seeker insofar as it seeks to create the fly or seeks to rescue what it took from them, and the sought is the fly. It has been said: the seeker is the worshipper of the idol, and the sought is the idol. It has also been said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the gods.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the polytheists who worshipped gods other than Allah, which are incapable to this extent of incapacity, did not know Allah with His true knowledge. So He said: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with His true esteem﴾. That is, they did not magnify Him with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, in that they made these idols partners to Him, while their condition is this condition. It has already been mentioned in *al-An'am* (surah 6): ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ over the creation of everything, ﴿Mighty, Overpowering﴾, whom no one can overpower, unlike the gods of the polytheists, for they are inanimate matter that do not reason, do not benefit, do not harm, and are not capable of anything.

Then He, glorified is He, intended to refute them regarding what they believe concerning prophethood and divinity, so He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels﴾, such as Jibril, Israfil, Mika'il, and 'Izra'il. He also chooses messengers from among mankind, who are the prophets. So He sends the angel to the prophet, and the prophet to people. Or He sends the angel to take the souls of His creatures, or to bring about what benefits them, or to send down punishment upon them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He chooses from among His creation.

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, that is, what they have sent forward of deeds and what they leave behind of good and evil, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:12]. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, not to other than Him.

Since what He mentioned contained that matters are returned to Him, it was a deterrent for His servants from their disobediences and an encouragement for them to His acts of obedience, He stated the purpose explicitly, so He said: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate﴾. That is, pray the prayer that Allah has legislated for you. He specified prayer because it is the most noble of the acts of worship.

Then He generalized, so He said: ﴿and worship your Lord﴾, that is, perform all kinds of worship that Allah has commanded you with. ﴿And do good﴾, that is, what is good, and it is more general than obligatory and recommended obedience. It has also been said: the intended good here is the recommended acts.

Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that you may succeed﴾. That is, if you do all of these, you hope for success.

This verse is among the places of prostration of recitation according to al-Shafi'i and those who agree with him, but not according to Abu Hanifah and those who say what he says. It has already been mentioned that this surah was given preference with two prostrations, and this is evidence for the legislation of prostration upon reciting this verse.

Then He commanded them with what is the peak of the religion and its greatest deeds, so He said: ﴿and strive for Allah﴾, that is, in His cause and for His sake. What is meant by it is the greater striving, which is the military campaign against the disbelievers and repelling them if they invade the lands of the Muslims.

It has also been said that what is meant by striving here is carrying out what Allah commanded them in the previous verse, or carrying out everything He commanded and forbade, in general. The meaning of ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾ is emphasis on the command of this striving, because He attributed the "due" (*haqq*) to the striving, whereas the original would be attributing the striving to the "due," i.e., striving sincerely for Allah. He reversed this for the purpose of emphasis. He attributed the striving to the pronoun for expansion, or because it is specific to Him, glorified is He, in that it is an object for Him and for His sake.

It has also been said: what is meant by "the due of His striving" is that you should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. It has been said: what is meant by it is exerting all of one's capacity in reviving the religion of Allah.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi (Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi, exegetes) said: the verse is abrogated (*mansukhah*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by His saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], just as His saying: ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:102] is abrogated by that. This was refuted on the basis that obligation is conditioned on capacity, so there is no need to resort to abrogation.

Then He, glorified is He, magnified the status of the responsible persons by His saying: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He selected you for His religion, and in this is a great honour for them.

Then, since in the obligation there is hardship upon the self in some states, He said: ﴿and He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾, that is, any narrowness or severity.

The scholars have differed regarding this hardship that Allah removed. It has been said: it is what Allah permitted of women, two, three, or four, and what the right hand possesses.

It has been said: what is meant is shortening the prayer, breaking the fast for the traveller, praying by gesture for the one who cannot pray otherwise, dropping striving from the lame, the blind, and the sick, excusing error in advancing or delaying the fast due to the differing of the crescent moons, and likewise at the Fitr and the Adha.

It has been said: the meaning is that He did not place upon them hardship by imposing what is difficult for them, but imposed upon them what they are able to do, and removed from them the obligations in which there is hardship, so He did not make them worship by them as He made the Children of Israel worship by them.

It has been said: what is meant by this is that He made for them an exit from sin by opening the door of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and expiation in what He legislated expiation and blood money for, or retaliation in injuries, and returning property or its equivalent or its value in usurpation and the like.

The apparent meaning is that the verse is more general than all of this. Glorified is He has removed from His servants what involves hardship of obligations, either by dropping them from the origin and not imposing them, as He imposed them on others, or by lightening them and permitting the substitution of something that involves no hardship, or by legislating the means to be freed from sin in the manner Allah has legislated. How beneficial this verse is, how great its place, and how immense its benefit! Similar to it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], and His saying: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:185], and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose upon us a burden as You imposed it upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:286].

In the authentic hadith, He, glorified is He, said: "I have done [that]," as its explanation has preceded in the tafsir of this verse. The hadiths on this are numerous.

The accusative of *millah* (religion, creed) in ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾ is as a verbal noun (*masdar*), governed by a verb implied by what precedes it, meaning: He has made your religion easy with the ease of the religion of your father Ibrahim. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, a grammarian) said: the meaning is "follow the religion of your father Ibrahim." Al-Farra' (al-Farra', a grammarian) said: it is in the accusative by way of the omitted particle *ka* (like), meaning: "like the religion of." It has been said: the estimate is: "and do good as the deed of your father Ibrahim," so he placed *millah* in place of the verb. It has been said: it is accusative by way of incitement (*al-ighra'*, urging someone toward something). It has been said: it is accusative by way of specification (*al-ikhtisas*).

He, glorified is He, made him their father only because he is the father of all the Arabs. Also, he has a great sanctity for non-Arabs who were not from his progeny, like the sanctity of a father upon a son, because he is the father of their prophet (ﷺ).

﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that is, in the earlier scriptures and in this [Qur'an]. The pronoun refers to Allah, glorified is He. It has been said: it refers back to Ibrahim.

The meaning is: he, that is Ibrahim, named you Muslims before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in this, that is in his ruling, that whoever follows Muhammad is a Muslim. Al-Nahhas said: this view contradicts the view of the scholars of the Ummah.

Then He, glorified is He, gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, that is, by his conveyance to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ that their messengers have conveyed to them. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has preceded in *al-Baqarah* (surah 2).

Then He commanded them with what is the greatest of the Islamic pillars, so He said: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾. The singling out of these two traits by mention is for their greater nobility. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾, that is, make Him your protection from what you fear, and seek refuge with Him in all your affairs, and seek that from none other than Him. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, that is, your helper and the one who manages your affairs, the subtle and the great of them. ﴿So excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾, that is, there is no equal to Him in being the guardian of your affairs and the one who gives victory over your enemies. It has been said: what is meant by His saying "hold fast to Allah" is: adhere to the religion of Allah. It has been said: trust in Him, exalted is He.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning an idol.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾, that he said: the seeker is their gods, and the sought is the fly.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿they cannot rescue it from it﴾, that he said: the idols cannot rescue that thing from the fly.

Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, also from him, from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah chose Musa with speech, and Ibrahim with intimate friendship."

He also narrated from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Musa ibn 'Imran is the chosen one (*safiyy*) of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar said to me: "Did we not used to recite, among what we recited: 'And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him' at the end of time, as you strove at its beginning?" I said: "Yes." He said: "When will that be, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "When the Banu Umayyah are the rulers and the Banu al-Mughirah are the viziers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in *al-Dala'il* from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: 'Umar said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and he mentioned it.

Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), Ibn Ḥibbān, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Askari in *al-Amthāl* narrated from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who strives (mujāhid) is the one who strives against his own self in obedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabarī), al-Ḥākim, who graded it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿĀʾishah that she asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about this verse, ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship (ḥaraj) in the religion﴾, and he said: "Ḥaraj is constriction (ḍayq)."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Muḥammad, who said: Abū Hurayrah said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Are we not under any hardship in the religion regarding whether we steal or commit adultery?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what is the meaning of ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾?" He said: "It is the burden (iṣr) that was upon the Children of Israel, which has been lifted from you."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of Ibn Shihāb that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: "﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ means the breadth (tawsiʿah) of Islam: what Allah has made of repentance and expiations (kaffārāt)."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of ʿUthmān ibn Yasār from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, that he said: "This applies to the crescent of Ramadan when people are in doubt about it, to the Ḥajj when they are in doubt about the Day of Sacrifice (al-Aḍḥā), to the Fiṭr (the end of Ramadan), and similar matters."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through the route of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj, and he said: "Call me a man from Hudhayl." A man came to him, and he said: "What is ḥaraj among you?" He said: "The ḥarijah is a tree (of thick growth) that has no way out (makhraj)." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "That which has no way out."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan* narrated through the route of ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abī Yazīd that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj and said: "Is there anyone here from Hudhayl?" A man said: "I am." He said: "What do you call ḥarijah among you?" He said: "The narrow thing." He said: "That is it."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 73–78 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined, so listen to it﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿and they worship, besides Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority﴾. Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, a grammarian) said: "There is no parable here. The meaning is: they coined a parable for Me, so listen to their statement." That is, the disbelievers made for Allah a likeness by worshipping other than Him. It is as if He said: "They made a likeness for Me in My worship, so listen to the account of this likeness."

Al-Qutaybi (al-Qutaybi, a lexicographer) said: "The meaning is: O mankind, the example of those who worship gods that cannot create a fly, and if it snatches something from them, they cannot rescue it from it."

Al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, a grammarian and exegete) said: "The meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, coined a parable for what they worship besides Him." He said: "This is among the best things said about it," i.e., Allah has explained to you a likeness, and to your deity.

The origin of a *mathal* (parable) is a sentence of speech that is received with approval and acceptance, circulated among people and regarded as remarkable. They made its source of coinage a parable for its occasion. Then they may borrow it for a story, a situation, or a quality that is remarkable, because it resembles it in strangeness, like this story mentioned in this verse.

What is meant by ﴿those they call upon besides Allah﴾ is the idols around the Ka'bah and others. It has also been said that it refers to the leaders who turned them away from obedience to Allah, because they were the people who loosed and bound among them. It has also been said that it refers to the devils who led them to disobey Allah. The first is more fitting to the context and clearer in the parable. *Al-dhubab* (the fly) is a noun for the single insect, used for both male and female. Its plural of paucity is *adhibbah*, and its plural of abundance is *dhibban*, like *ghurab* (crow), *aghribah*, and *ghirban*.

Al-Jawhari (al-Jawhari, a lexicographer) said: "*Al-dhubab* is well known; its singular is *dhubabah*." The meaning is: they will not be able to create it, despite its being small in body and insignificant in essence.

The clause ﴿and if they gathered together for it﴾ is conjoined to another conditional clause that is omitted, meaning: "If they did not gather for it, they would not create it, and even if they gathered for it." The response is omitted, and the estimate is: "they will not create it." Both clauses are in the accusative position as a circumstantial state, meaning: they will not create it in any state.

Then He, glorified is He, explained the completeness of their incapacity and the weakness of their power, so He said: ﴿and if the fly snatches from them anything, they cannot rescue it from it﴾. That is, if the fly takes from them anything of things, they are unable to free it from it, because of the completeness of their incapacity and the extreme of their weakness. *Al-istinqadh* and *al-inqadh* mean rescue and deliverance. If they are unable to create this weak creature, and unable to rescue what it took from them, then they are more incapable and weaker regarding something other than it that is greater in body and stronger in power.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the weakness of the idols and the fly, so He said: ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾. The idol is like the seeker insofar as it seeks to create the fly or seeks to rescue what it took from them, and the sought is the fly. It has been said: the seeker is the worshipper of the idol, and the sought is the idol. It has also been said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the gods.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the polytheists who worshipped gods other than Allah, which are incapable to this extent of incapacity, did not know Allah with His true knowledge. So He said: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with His true esteem﴾. That is, they did not magnify Him with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, in that they made these idols partners to Him, while their condition is this condition. It has already been mentioned in *al-An'am* (surah 6): ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ over the creation of everything, ﴿Mighty, Overpowering﴾, whom no one can overpower, unlike the gods of the polytheists, for they are inanimate matter that do not reason, do not benefit, do not harm, and are not capable of anything.

Then He, glorified is He, intended to refute them regarding what they believe concerning prophethood and divinity, so He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels﴾, such as Jibril, Israfil, Mika'il, and 'Izra'il. He also chooses messengers from among mankind, who are the prophets. So He sends the angel to the prophet, and the prophet to people. Or He sends the angel to take the souls of His creatures, or to bring about what benefits them, or to send down punishment upon them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He chooses from among His creation.

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, that is, what they have sent forward of deeds and what they leave behind of good and evil, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:12]. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, not to other than Him.

Since what He mentioned contained that matters are returned to Him, it was a deterrent for His servants from their disobediences and an encouragement for them to His acts of obedience, He stated the purpose explicitly, so He said: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate﴾. That is, pray the prayer that Allah has legislated for you. He specified prayer because it is the most noble of the acts of worship.

Then He generalized, so He said: ﴿and worship your Lord﴾, that is, perform all kinds of worship that Allah has commanded you with. ﴿And do good﴾, that is, what is good, and it is more general than obligatory and recommended obedience. It has also been said: the intended good here is the recommended acts.

Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that you may succeed﴾. That is, if you do all of these, you hope for success.

This verse is among the places of prostration of recitation according to al-Shafi'i and those who agree with him, but not according to Abu Hanifah and those who say what he says. It has already been mentioned that this surah was given preference with two prostrations, and this is evidence for the legislation of prostration upon reciting this verse.

Then He commanded them with what is the peak of the religion and its greatest deeds, so He said: ﴿and strive for Allah﴾, that is, in His cause and for His sake. What is meant by it is the greater striving, which is the military campaign against the disbelievers and repelling them if they invade the lands of the Muslims.

It has also been said that what is meant by striving here is carrying out what Allah commanded them in the previous verse, or carrying out everything He commanded and forbade, in general. The meaning of ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾ is emphasis on the command of this striving, because He attributed the "due" (*haqq*) to the striving, whereas the original would be attributing the striving to the "due," i.e., striving sincerely for Allah. He reversed this for the purpose of emphasis. He attributed the striving to the pronoun for expansion, or because it is specific to Him, glorified is He, in that it is an object for Him and for His sake.

It has also been said: what is meant by "the due of His striving" is that you should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. It has been said: what is meant by it is exerting all of one's capacity in reviving the religion of Allah.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi (Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi, exegetes) said: the verse is abrogated (*mansukhah*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by His saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], just as His saying: ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:102] is abrogated by that. This was refuted on the basis that obligation is conditioned on capacity, so there is no need to resort to abrogation.

Then He, glorified is He, magnified the status of the responsible persons by His saying: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He selected you for His religion, and in this is a great honour for them.

Then, since in the obligation there is hardship upon the self in some states, He said: ﴿and He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾, that is, any narrowness or severity.

The scholars have differed regarding this hardship that Allah removed. It has been said: it is what Allah permitted of women, two, three, or four, and what the right hand possesses.

It has been said: what is meant is shortening the prayer, breaking the fast for the traveller, praying by gesture for the one who cannot pray otherwise, dropping striving from the lame, the blind, and the sick, excusing error in advancing or delaying the fast due to the differing of the crescent moons, and likewise at the Fitr and the Adha.

It has been said: the meaning is that He did not place upon them hardship by imposing what is difficult for them, but imposed upon them what they are able to do, and removed from them the obligations in which there is hardship, so He did not make them worship by them as He made the Children of Israel worship by them.

It has been said: what is meant by this is that He made for them an exit from sin by opening the door of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and expiation in what He legislated expiation and blood money for, or retaliation in injuries, and returning property or its equivalent or its value in usurpation and the like.

The apparent meaning is that the verse is more general than all of this. Glorified is He has removed from His servants what involves hardship of obligations, either by dropping them from the origin and not imposing them, as He imposed them on others, or by lightening them and permitting the substitution of something that involves no hardship, or by legislating the means to be freed from sin in the manner Allah has legislated. How beneficial this verse is, how great its place, and how immense its benefit! Similar to it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], and His saying: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:185], and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose upon us a burden as You imposed it upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:286].

In the authentic hadith, He, glorified is He, said: "I have done [that]," as its explanation has preceded in the tafsir of this verse. The hadiths on this are numerous.

The accusative of *millah* (religion, creed) in ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾ is as a verbal noun (*masdar*), governed by a verb implied by what precedes it, meaning: He has made your religion easy with the ease of the religion of your father Ibrahim. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, a grammarian) said: the meaning is "follow the religion of your father Ibrahim." Al-Farra' (al-Farra', a grammarian) said: it is in the accusative by way of the omitted particle *ka* (like), meaning: "like the religion of." It has been said: the estimate is: "and do good as the deed of your father Ibrahim," so he placed *millah* in place of the verb. It has been said: it is accusative by way of incitement (*al-ighra'*, urging someone toward something). It has been said: it is accusative by way of specification (*al-ikhtisas*).

He, glorified is He, made him their father only because he is the father of all the Arabs. Also, he has a great sanctity for non-Arabs who were not from his progeny, like the sanctity of a father upon a son, because he is the father of their prophet (ﷺ).

﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that is, in the earlier scriptures and in this [Qur'an]. The pronoun refers to Allah, glorified is He. It has been said: it refers back to Ibrahim.

The meaning is: he, that is Ibrahim, named you Muslims before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in this, that is in his ruling, that whoever follows Muhammad is a Muslim. Al-Nahhas said: this view contradicts the view of the scholars of the Ummah.

Then He, glorified is He, gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, that is, by his conveyance to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ that their messengers have conveyed to them. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has preceded in *al-Baqarah* (surah 2).

Then He commanded them with what is the greatest of the Islamic pillars, so He said: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾. The singling out of these two traits by mention is for their greater nobility. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾, that is, make Him your protection from what you fear, and seek refuge with Him in all your affairs, and seek that from none other than Him. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, that is, your helper and the one who manages your affairs, the subtle and the great of them. ﴿So excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾, that is, there is no equal to Him in being the guardian of your affairs and the one who gives victory over your enemies. It has been said: what is meant by His saying "hold fast to Allah" is: adhere to the religion of Allah. It has been said: trust in Him, exalted is He.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning an idol.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾, that he said: the seeker is their gods, and the sought is the fly.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿they cannot rescue it from it﴾, that he said: the idols cannot rescue that thing from the fly.

Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, also from him, from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah chose Musa with speech, and Ibrahim with intimate friendship."

He also narrated from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Musa ibn 'Imran is the chosen one (*safiyy*) of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar said to me: "Did we not used to recite, among what we recited: 'And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him' at the end of time, as you strove at its beginning?" I said: "Yes." He said: "When will that be, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "When the Banu Umayyah are the rulers and the Banu al-Mughirah are the viziers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in *al-Dala'il* from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: 'Umar said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and he mentioned it.

Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), Ibn Ḥibbān, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Askari in *al-Amthāl* narrated from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who strives (mujāhid) is the one who strives against his own self in obedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabarī), al-Ḥākim, who graded it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿĀʾishah that she asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about this verse, ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship (ḥaraj) in the religion﴾, and he said: "Ḥaraj is constriction (ḍayq)."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Muḥammad, who said: Abū Hurayrah said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Are we not under any hardship in the religion regarding whether we steal or commit adultery?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what is the meaning of ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾?" He said: "It is the burden (iṣr) that was upon the Children of Israel, which has been lifted from you."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of Ibn Shihāb that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: "﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ means the breadth (tawsiʿah) of Islam: what Allah has made of repentance and expiations (kaffārāt)."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of ʿUthmān ibn Yasār from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, that he said: "This applies to the crescent of Ramadan when people are in doubt about it, to the Ḥajj when they are in doubt about the Day of Sacrifice (al-Aḍḥā), to the Fiṭr (the end of Ramadan), and similar matters."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through the route of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj, and he said: "Call me a man from Hudhayl." A man came to him, and he said: "What is ḥaraj among you?" He said: "The ḥarijah is a tree (of thick growth) that has no way out (makhraj)." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "That which has no way out."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan* narrated through the route of ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abī Yazīd that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj and said: "Is there anyone here from Hudhayl?" A man said: "I am." He said: "What do you call ḥarijah among you?" He said: "The narrow thing." He said: "That is it."

He attributed the striving to the pronoun for expansion, or because it is specific to Him, glorified is He, in that it is an object for Him and for His sake.

It has also been said: what is meant by "the due of His striving" is that you should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. It has been said: what is meant by it is exerting all of one's capacity in reviving the religion of Allah.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi (Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi, exegetes) said: the verse is abrogated (*mansukhah*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by His saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], just as His saying: ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:102] is abrogated by that. This was refuted on the basis that obligation is conditioned on capacity, so there is no need to resort to abrogation.

Then He, glorified is He, magnified the status of the responsible persons by His saying: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He selected you for His religion, and in this is a great honour for them.

Then, since in the obligation there is hardship upon the self in some states, He said: ﴿and He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾, that is, any narrowness or severity.

The scholars have differed regarding this hardship that Allah removed. It has been said: it is what Allah permitted of women, two, three, or four, and what the right hand possesses.

It has been said: what is meant is shortening the prayer, breaking the fast for the traveller, praying by gesture for the one who cannot pray otherwise, dropping striving from the lame, the blind, and the sick, excusing error in advancing or delaying the fast due to the differing of the crescent moons, and likewise at the Fitr and the Adha.

It has been said: the meaning is that He did not place upon them hardship by imposing what is difficult for them, but imposed upon them what they are able to do, and removed from them the obligations in which there is hardship, so He did not make them worship by them as He made the Children of Israel worship by them.

It has been said: what is meant by this is that He made for them an exit from sin by opening the door of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and expiation in what He legislated expiation and blood money for, or retaliation in injuries, and returning property or its equivalent or its value in usurpation and the like.

The apparent meaning is that the verse is more general than all of this. Glorified is He has removed from His servants what involves hardship of obligations, either by dropping them from the origin and not imposing them, as He imposed them on others, or by lightening them and permitting the substitution of something that involves no hardship, or by legislating the means to be freed from sin in the manner Allah has legislated. How beneficial this verse is, how great its place, and how immense its benefit! Similar to it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], and His saying: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:185], and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose upon us a burden as You imposed it upon those before us. In the authentic hadith, He, glorified is He, said: "I have done [that]," as its explanation has preceded in the tafsir of this verse. The hadiths on this are numerous.

The accusative of *millah* (religion, creed) in ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾ is as a verbal noun (*masdar*), governed by a verb implied by what precedes it, meaning: He has made your religion easy with the ease of the religion of your father Ibrahim. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, a grammarian) said: the meaning is "follow the religion of your father Ibrahim." Al-Farra' (al-Farra', a grammarian) said: it is in the accusative by way of the omitted particle *ka* (like), meaning: "like the religion of." It has been said: the estimate is: "and do good as the deed of your father Ibrahim," so he placed *millah* in place of the verb. It has been said: it is accusative by way of incitement (*al-ighra'*, urging someone toward something). It has been said: it is accusative by way of specification (*al-ikhtisas*).

He, glorified is He, made him their father only because he is the father of all the Arabs. Also, he has a great sanctity for non-Arabs who were not from his progeny, like the sanctity of a father upon a son, because he is the father of their prophet (ﷺ).

﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that is, in the earlier scriptures and in this [Qur'an]. The pronoun refers to Allah, glorified is He. It has been said: it refers back to Ibrahim.

The meaning is: he, that is Ibrahim, named you Muslims before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in this, that is in his ruling, that whoever follows Muhammad is a Muslim. Al-Nahhas said: this view contradicts the view of the scholars of the Ummah.

Then He, glorified is He, gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, that is, by his conveyance to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ that their messengers have conveyed to them. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has preceded in *al-Baqarah* (surah 2).

Then He commanded them with what is the greatest of the Islamic pillars, so He said: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾. The singling out of these two traits by mention is for their greater nobility. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾, that is, make Him your protection from what you fear, and seek refuge with Him in all your affairs, and seek that from none other than Him. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, that is, your helper and the one who manages your affairs, the subtle and the great of them. ﴿So excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾, that is, there is no equal to Him in being the guardian of your affairs and the one who gives victory over your enemies. It has been said: what is meant by His saying "hold fast to Allah" is: adhere to the religion of Allah. It has been said: trust in Him, exalted is He.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning an idol.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾, that he said: the seeker is their gods, and the sought is the fly.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿they cannot rescue it from it﴾, that he said: the idols cannot rescue that thing from the fly.

Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, also from him, from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah chose Musa with speech, and Ibrahim with intimate friendship."

He also narrated from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Musa ibn 'Imran is the chosen one (*safiyy*) of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar said to me: "Did we not used to recite, among what we recited: 'And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him' at the end of time, as you strove at its beginning?" I said: "Yes." He said: "When will that be, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "When the Banu Umayyah are the rulers and the Banu al-Mughirah are the viziers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in *al-Dala'il* from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: 'Umar said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and he mentioned it.

Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), Ibn Ḥibbān, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Askari in *al-Amthāl* narrated from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who strives (mujāhid) is the one who strives against his own self in obedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabarī), al-Ḥākim, who graded it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿĀʾishah that she asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about this verse, ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship (ḥaraj) in the religion﴾, and he said: "Ḥaraj is constriction (ḍayq)."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Muḥammad, who said: Abū Hurayrah said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Are we not under any hardship in the religion regarding whether we steal or commit adultery?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what is the meaning of ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾?" He said: "It is the burden (iṣr) that was upon the Children of Israel, which has been lifted from you."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of Ibn Shihāb that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: "﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ means the breadth (tawsiʿah) of Islam: what Allah has made of repentance and expiations (kaffārāt)."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through the route of ʿUthmān ibn Yasār from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, that he said: "This applies to the crescent of Ramadan when people are in doubt about it, to the Ḥajj when they are in doubt about the Day of Sacrifice (al-Aḍḥā), to the Fiṭr (the end of Ramadan), and similar matters."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through the route of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj, and he said: "Call me a man from Hudhayl." A man came to him, and he said: "What is ḥaraj among you?" He said: "The ḥarijah is a tree (of thick growth) that has no way out (makhraj)." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "That which has no way out."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan* narrated through the route of ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abī Yazīd that Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about ḥaraj and said: "Is there anyone here from Hudhayl?" A man said: "I am." He said: "What do you call ḥarijah among you?" He said: "The narrow thing." He said: "That is it."

Al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan* narrated from Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb recited this verse, ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾, then said to me: "Call me a man from Banū Mudlij." ʿUmar said: "What is ḥaraj among you?" He said: "Constriction (al-ḍayq)."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from al-Suddī regarding His words, ﴿the religion of your father (millata abīkum)﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated through several routes from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words, ﴿He named you "Muslims" before (min qabl)﴾: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, named you." A similar report is related from a group of the Successors (tābiʿūn).

Al-Ṭayālisī, Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī in his *Tārīkh*, al-Tirmidhī, who graded it sound, al-Nasāʾī, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Baghawī, al-Bārūdī, Ibn Qāniʿ, al-Ṭabarānī, al-Ḥākim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in *Shuʿab al-Īmān* narrated from al-Ḥārith al-Ashʿarī, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever calls with the call of the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance), he is of the kneeling-crowd (juthiyy) of Hell." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he fasts and prays?" He said: "Yes. So call with the call of Allah, with which He named you Muslims and believers, the servants of Allah."

His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined, so listen to it﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿and they worship, besides Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority﴾. Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, a grammarian) said: "There is no parable here. The meaning is: they coined a parable for Me, so listen to their statement." That is, the disbelievers made for Allah a likeness by worshipping other than Him. It is as if He said: "They made a likeness for Me in My worship, so listen to the account of this likeness."

Al-Qutaybi (al-Qutaybi, a lexicographer) said: "The meaning is: O mankind, the example of those who worship gods that cannot create a fly, and if it snatches something from them, they cannot rescue it from it."

Al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, a grammarian and exegete) said: "The meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, coined a parable for what they worship besides Him." He said: "This is among the best things said about it," i.e., Allah has explained to you a likeness, and to your deity.

The origin of a *mathal* (parable) is a sentence of speech that is received with approval and acceptance, circulated among people and regarded as remarkable. They made its source of coinage a parable for its occasion. Then they may borrow it for a story, a situation, or a quality that is remarkable, because it resembles it in strangeness, like this story mentioned in this verse.

What is meant by ﴿those they call upon besides Allah﴾ is the idols around the Ka'bah and others. It has also been said that it refers to the leaders who turned them away from obedience to Allah, because they were the people who loosed and bound among them. It has also been said that it refers to the devils who led them to disobey Allah. The first is more fitting to the context and clearer in the parable. *Al-dhubab* (the fly) is a noun for the single insect, used for both male and female. Its plural of paucity is *adhibbah*, and its plural of abundance is *dhibban*, like *ghurab* (crow), *aghribah*, and *ghirban*.

Al-Jawhari (al-Jawhari, a lexicographer) said: "*Al-dhubab* is well known; its singular is *dhubabah*." The meaning is: they will not be able to create it, despite its being small in body and insignificant in essence.

The clause ﴿and if they gathered together for it﴾ is conjoined to another conditional clause that is omitted, meaning: "If they did not gather for it, they would not create it, and even if they gathered for it." The response is omitted, and the estimate is: "they will not create it." Both clauses are in the accusative position as a circumstantial state, meaning: they will not create it in any state.

Then He, glorified is He, explained the completeness of their incapacity and the weakness of their power, so He said: ﴿and if the fly snatches from them anything, they cannot rescue it from it﴾. That is, if the fly takes from them anything of things, they are unable to free it from it, because of the completeness of their incapacity and the extreme of their weakness. *Al-istinqadh* and *al-inqadh* mean rescue and deliverance. If they are unable to create this weak creature, and unable to rescue what it took from them, then they are more incapable and weaker regarding something other than it that is greater in body and stronger in power.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the weakness of the idols and the fly, so He said: ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾. The idol is like the seeker insofar as it seeks to create the fly or seeks to rescue what it took from them, and the sought is the fly. It has been said: the seeker is the worshipper of the idol, and the sought is the idol. It has also been said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the gods.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the polytheists who worshipped gods other than Allah, which are incapable to this extent of incapacity, did not know Allah with His true knowledge. So He said: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with His true esteem﴾. That is, they did not magnify Him with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, in that they made these idols partners to Him, while their condition is this condition. It has already been mentioned in *al-An'am* (surah 6): ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ over the creation of everything, ﴿Mighty, Overpowering﴾, whom no one can overpower, unlike the gods of the polytheists, for they are inanimate matter that do not reason, do not benefit, do not harm, and are not capable of anything.

Then He, glorified is He, intended to refute them regarding what they believe concerning prophethood and divinity, so He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels﴾, such as Jibril, Israfil, Mika'il, and 'Izra'il. He also chooses messengers from among mankind, who are the prophets. So He sends the angel to the prophet, and the prophet to people. Or He sends the angel to take the souls of His creatures, or to bring about what benefits them, or to send down punishment upon them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He chooses from among His creation.

It has also been said: the intended good here is the recommended acts.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 22, verses 73–78 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined, so listen to it﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿and they worship, besides Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority﴾. Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, a grammarian) said: "There is no parable here. The meaning is: they coined a parable for Me, so listen to their statement." That is, the disbelievers made for Allah a likeness by worshipping other than Him. It is as if He said: "They made a likeness for Me in My worship, so listen to the account of this likeness."

Al-Qutaybi (al-Qutaybi, a lexicographer) said: "The meaning is: O mankind, the example of those who worship gods that cannot create a fly, and if it snatches something from them, they cannot rescue it from it."

Al-Nahhas (al-Nahhas, a grammarian and exegete) said: "The meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, coined a parable for what they worship besides Him." He said: "This is among the best things said about it," i.e., Allah has explained to you a likeness, and to your deity.

The origin of a *mathal* (parable) is a sentence of speech that is received with approval and acceptance, circulated among people and regarded as remarkable. They made its source of coinage a parable for its occasion. Then they may borrow it for a story, a situation, or a quality that is remarkable, because it resembles it in strangeness, like this story mentioned in this verse.

What is meant by ﴿those they call upon besides Allah﴾ is the idols around the Ka'bah and others. It has also been said that it refers to the leaders who turned them away from obedience to Allah, because they were the people who loosed and bound among them. It has also been said that it refers to the devils who led them to disobey Allah. The first is more fitting to the context and clearer in the parable. *Al-dhubab* (the fly) is a noun for the single insect, used for both male and female. Its plural of paucity is *adhibbah*, and its plural of abundance is *dhibban*, like *ghurab* (crow), *aghribah*, and *ghirban*.

Al-Jawhari (al-Jawhari, a lexicographer) said: "*Al-dhubab* is well known; its singular is *dhubabah*." The meaning is: they will not be able to create it, despite its being small in body and insignificant in essence.

The clause ﴿and if they gathered together for it﴾ is conjoined to another conditional clause that is omitted, meaning: "If they did not gather for it, they would not create it, and even if they gathered for it." The response is omitted, and the estimate is: "they will not create it." Both clauses are in the accusative position as a circumstantial state, meaning: they will not create it in any state.

Then He, glorified is He, explained the completeness of their incapacity and the weakness of their power, so He said: ﴿and if the fly snatches from them anything, they cannot rescue it from it﴾. That is, if the fly takes from them anything of things, they are unable to free it from it, because of the completeness of their incapacity and the extreme of their weakness. *Al-istinqadh* and *al-inqadh* mean rescue and deliverance. If they are unable to create this weak creature, and unable to rescue what it took from them, then they are more incapable and weaker regarding something other than it that is greater in body and stronger in power.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the weakness of the idols and the fly, so He said: ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾. The idol is like the seeker insofar as it seeks to create the fly or seeks to rescue what it took from them, and the sought is the fly. It has been said: the seeker is the worshipper of the idol, and the sought is the idol. It has also been said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the gods.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the polytheists who worshipped gods other than Allah, which are incapable to this extent of incapacity, did not know Allah with His true knowledge. So He said: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with His true esteem﴾. That is, they did not magnify Him with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, in that they made these idols partners to Him, while their condition is this condition. It has already been mentioned in *al-An'am* (surah 6): ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ over the creation of everything, ﴿Mighty, Overpowering﴾, whom no one can overpower, unlike the gods of the polytheists, for they are inanimate matter that do not reason, do not benefit, do not harm, and are not capable of anything.

Then He, glorified is He, intended to refute them regarding what they believe concerning prophethood and divinity, so He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels﴾, such as Jibril, Israfil, Mika'il, and 'Izra'il. He also chooses messengers from among mankind, who are the prophets. So He sends the angel to the prophet, and the prophet to people. Or He sends the angel to take the souls of His creatures, or to bring about what benefits them, or to send down punishment upon them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of His servants, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He chooses from among His creation.

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, that is, what they have sent forward of deeds and what they leave behind of good and evil, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:12]. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, not to other than Him.

Since what He mentioned contained that matters are returned to Him, it was a deterrent for His servants from their disobediences and an encouragement for them to His acts of obedience, He stated the purpose explicitly, so He said: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate﴾. That is, pray the prayer that Allah has legislated for you. He specified prayer because it is the most noble of the acts of worship.

Then He generalized, so He said: ﴿and worship your Lord﴾, that is, perform all kinds of worship that Allah has commanded you with. ﴿And do good﴾, that is, what is good, and it is more general than obligatory and recommended obedience. It has also been said: the intended good here is the recommended acts.

Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that you may succeed﴾. That is, if you do all of these, you hope for success.

This verse is among the places of prostration of recitation according to al-Shafi'i and those who agree with him, but not according to Abu Hanifah and those who say what he says. It has already been mentioned that this surah was given preference with two prostrations, and this is evidence for the legislation of prostration upon reciting this verse.

Then He commanded them with what is the peak of the religion and its greatest deeds, so He said: ﴿and strive for Allah﴾, that is, in His cause and for His sake. What is meant by it is the greater striving, which is the military campaign against the disbelievers and repelling them if they invade the lands of the Muslims.

It has also been said that what is meant by striving here is carrying out what Allah commanded them in the previous verse, or carrying out everything He commanded and forbade, in general. The meaning of ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾ is emphasis on the command of this striving, because He attributed the "due" (*haqq*) to the striving, whereas the original would be attributing the striving to the "due," i.e., striving sincerely for Allah. He reversed this for the purpose of emphasis. He attributed the striving to the pronoun for expansion, or because it is specific to Him, glorified is He, in that it is an object for Him and for His sake.

It has also been said: what is meant by "the due of His striving" is that you should not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. It has been said: what is meant by it is exerting all of one's capacity in reviving the religion of Allah.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi (Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi, exegetes) said: the verse is abrogated (*mansukhah*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by His saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], just as His saying: ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:102] is abrogated by that. This was refuted on the basis that obligation is conditioned on capacity, so there is no need to resort to abrogation.

Then He, glorified is He, magnified the status of the responsible persons by His saying: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He selected you for His religion, and in this is a great honour for them.

Then, since in the obligation there is hardship upon the self in some states, He said: ﴿and He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾, that is, any narrowness or severity.

The scholars have differed regarding this hardship that Allah removed. It has been said: it is what Allah permitted of women, two, three, or four, and what the right hand possesses.

It has been said: what is meant is shortening the prayer, breaking the fast for the traveller, praying by gesture for the one who cannot pray otherwise, dropping striving from the lame, the blind, and the sick, excusing error in advancing or delaying the fast due to the differing of the crescent moons, and likewise at the Fitr and the Adha.

It has been said: the meaning is that He did not place upon them hardship by imposing what is difficult for them, but imposed upon them what they are able to do, and removed from them the obligations in which there is hardship, so He did not make them worship by them as He made the Children of Israel worship by them.

It has been said: what is meant by this is that He made for them an exit from sin by opening the door of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and expiation in what He legislated expiation and blood money for, or retaliation in injuries, and returning property or its equivalent or its value in usurpation and the like.

The apparent meaning is that the verse is more general than all of this. Glorified is He has removed from His servants what involves hardship of obligations, either by dropping them from the origin and not imposing them, as He imposed them on others, or by lightening them and permitting the substitution of something that involves no hardship, or by legislating the means to be freed from sin in the manner Allah has legislated. How beneficial this verse is, how great its place, and how immense its benefit! Similar to it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16], and His saying: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:185], and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose upon us a burden as You imposed it upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:286].

In the authentic hadith, He, glorified is He, said: "I have done [that]," as its explanation has preceded in the tafsir of this verse. The hadiths on this are numerous.

The accusative of *millah* (religion, creed) in ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾ is as a verbal noun (*masdar*), governed by a verb implied by what precedes it, meaning: He has made your religion easy with the ease of the religion of your father Ibrahim. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, a grammarian) said: the meaning is "follow the religion of your father Ibrahim." Al-Farra' (al-Farra', a grammarian) said: it is in the accusative by way of the omitted particle *ka* (like), meaning: "like the religion of." It has been said: the estimate is: "and do good as the deed of your father Ibrahim," so he placed *millah* in place of the verb. It has been said: it is accusative by way of incitement (*al-ighra'*, urging someone toward something). It has been said: it is accusative by way of specification (*al-ikhtisas*).

He, glorified is He, made him their father only because he is the father of all the Arabs. Also, he has a great sanctity for non-Arabs who were not from his progeny, like the sanctity of a father upon a son, because he is the father of their prophet (ﷺ).

﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, that is, in the earlier scriptures and in this [Qur'an]. The pronoun refers to Allah, glorified is He. It has been said: it refers back to Ibrahim.

The meaning is: he, that is Ibrahim, named you Muslims before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in this, that is in his ruling, that whoever follows Muhammad is a Muslim. Al-Nahhas said: this view contradicts the view of the scholars of the Ummah.

Then He, glorified is He, gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, that is, by his conveyance to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ that their messengers have conveyed to them. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has preceded in *al-Baqarah* (surah 2).

Then He commanded them with what is the greatest of the Islamic pillars, so He said: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah﴾. The singling out of these two traits by mention is for their greater nobility. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾, that is, make Him your protection from what you fear, and seek refuge with Him in all your affairs, and seek that from none other than Him. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, that is, your helper and the one who manages your affairs, the subtle and the great of them. ﴿So excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper﴾, that is, there is no equal to Him in being the guardian of your affairs and the one who gives victory over your enemies. It has been said: what is meant by His saying "hold fast to Allah" is: adhere to the religion of Allah. It has been said: trust in Him, exalted is He.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning an idol.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾, that he said: the seeker is their gods, and the sought is the fly.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿they cannot rescue it from it﴾, that he said: the idols cannot rescue that thing from the fly.

Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, also from him, from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah chose Musa with speech, and Ibrahim with intimate friendship."

He also narrated from Anas, and he authenticated it, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Musa ibn 'Imran is the chosen one (*safiyy*) of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar said to me: "Did we not used to recite, among what we recited: 'And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him' at the end of time, as you strove at its beginning?" I said: "Yes." He said: "When will that be, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "When the Banu Umayyah are the rulers and the Banu al-Mughirah are the viziers."
